That one difference explains most of what confuses people about AI, so this part goes slowly. Think of it as the slow lane. I promise there's no quiz. Okay, one small quiz, at the very end, and you already know the answer. The model: an engine A language model is a very large mathematical function. You give it text, and it returns its best guess at the next small piece of text, called a token (roughly three-quarters of a word). Then it adds that token to the input and guesses again, over and over, until the answer is finished. Almost every modern model is built on a design called the Transformer , introduced in 2017 [1] . Its key idea is attention : for every word, the model weighs how much each other word in the passage matters to it. In "The trophy didn't fit in the suitcase because it was too big," attention is how the model works out that "it" means the trophy. (The suitcase had no comment.) Analogy: autocomplete on your phone is a model the size of a pocket calculator. x: Earbud Sound Lab: why fit changes bass | LeonLink Sound Lab Why fit makes bass Same earbuds, two people: one hears thumping bass, the other hears thin and tinny. Usually it isn't the earbuds. It's the seal. Try it below on your phone, with your earbuds in. Start with your volume low. Every tone here is gentle, but your device volume is in charge. Step 1 Sound is air being pushed A speaker pushes air back and forth. How many times a second is the frequency : low numbers are bass you feel, high numbers are hiss and sparkle. Slide it and watch the wave. Frequency 200 Hz ▶ Play tone Bass waves are long : a 50 Hz wave is almost 7 metres from peak to peak. A tiny earbud driver can't fill a room with that. It makes bass by pressurising the small sealed space in your ear canal. Step 2 A leak lets the bass escape When the tip seals, the air in your ear canal has nowhere to go, so a tiny push becomes real pressure on your eardrum. Open a gap and the low notes leak out first, while high notes barely notice. Hear it: Seal Perfect seal ▶ Play beat Slide toward "Loose" while it plays A filter simulates the leak. The green line shows how loud each frequency reaches your eardrum. That's also why noise cancelling needs a seal. If outside noise sneaks around the tip, the earbud can't cancel what it can't control. Step 3 Test your own fit Earbuds in. Tap each tone. T100 Swiss tritium ~12.3 yr half-life 0 charging How it works Tiny glass tubes that light themselves A tritium watch has tiny sealed glass tubes on its hands and markers. Each holds a little tritium gas, a radioactive form of hydrogen, and is coated inside with phosphor. As the tritium decays it gives off weak electrons that hit the phosphor and make it glow. No sunlight, no charging, no button. Regular glow paint soaks up light and lets it out slowly: bright at first, dim a few hours later. The glow slowly dims as the tritium decays, losing about half its brightness roughly every 12 years. Is it safe? The electrons can't even get through the glass tube, let alone the case and crystal.
